chief_complaint: watery burning red eye with tender preauricular node
hpi_details: A 50-year-old female presents to the clinic with watery burning red eye with tender preauricular node. The patient states the symptoms started recently and have been gradually worsening, accompanied by generalized fatigue.
ideas: She thinks she caught a bad cold bug that got into her eye, especially since she has been feeling run down and exhausted lately.
concerns: She is worried that the tender lump in front of her ear is a cancerous lymph node or tumor.
expectations: She hopes to receive prescription antibiotic eye drops and medication to clear up the redness quickly.

core_concepts: Prompt recognition and structured assessment of Adenoviral conjunctivitis is essential for guiding targeted diagnostic workup and clinical decision-making.
A thorough clinical history, baseline risk assessment, and targeted objective testing must be synthesized rather than relying on any single symptom in isolation.
Standard management emphasizes Plan for Adenoviral Conjunctivitis: Symptomatic artificial tears, cool compresses, hand washing, adapted to individual patient risk factors and clinical severity.
Diagnostic workup and therapeutic decisions should adhere to established clinical guidelines while accounting for patient-specific comorbidities.

common_misconceptions: Assuming that an atypical or mild presentation rules out Adenoviral conjunctivitis.
Relying solely on a single normal laboratory value or imaging result to prematurely exclude pathology.
Equating temporary symptomatic relief with full resolution of the underlying condition without completing standard evaluation.
Misattributing symptoms exclusively to Bacterial conjunctivitis without completing a comprehensive diagnostic workup.
dangerous_errors: Failing to recognize red-flag features and delaying urgent escalation or emergency intervention.
Prematurely discharging or reassuring the patient before completing appropriate diagnostic assessment.
Initiating empirical treatment without considering major patient contraindications or drug interactions.
Ignoring critical warning signs such as: Highly contagious — spread precautions essential.
management_principles: Plan for Adenoviral Conjunctivitis: Symptomatic artificial tears, cool compresses, hand washing
Urgently assess or refer for reduced visual acuity, significant pain or photophobia, corneal opacity, contact-lens-associated red eye, or suspected herpes infection
boundaries_and_exceptions: Specific drug dosages, monitoring protocols, and referral criteria must be tailored to organ function, comorbidities, and local hospital pathways.
Atypical presentations in elderly, pediatric, or immunocompromised patients may require lower thresholds for inpatient monitoring and specialist consultation.

reference_soap.subjective: Patient presenting with chief complaint of watery burning red eye with tender preauricular node. HPI: adenoviral conjunctivitis.
reference_soap.objective: Focused physical exam and vital signs check. Tailored diagnostics for Adenoviral Conjunctivitis.
reference_soap.assessment: Condition highly suspicious for Adenoviral Conjunctivitis.
reference_soap.plan: Provide preservative-free artificial tears, cool compresses, and strict hand, towel, and cosmetic hygiene; avoid sharing personal items. Check visual acuity and refer urgently for reduced vision, marked pain or photophobia, corneal findings, contact-lens-associated red eye, or suspected herpes infection.

teaching.one_liner: Patient with a watery, burning red eye and a tender preauricular lymph node.

must_ask.objective: Screen for sight-threatening red-eye features and contact-lens risk
must_ask.say: Is your vision reduced, do you have significant pain or light sensitivity, and do you wear contact lenses?
Is the discharge watery and clear, rather than thick and colored?

must_ask.objective: Ask about the tender lump near the ear
must_ask.say: Do you feel a tender lump in front of your ear?

must_ask.objective: Ask about recent illness or sick contacts
must_ask.say: Have you been sick recently or around anyone with pink eye?
Did this start in one eye and spread to the other?

must_ask.objective: Explain supportive care and hygiene precautions
must_ask.say: This is viral, so we'll use supportive care like cool compresses, and it's very important to wash your hands frequently.

history.answer: My right eye has been red, burning, and constantly watering for the last three days, and I noticed a tender lump right in front of my ear.
It started three days ago with burning and watery tears in my right eye, and it has gradually become redder and more irritated since then.
It was only in my right eye at first, but just this morning my left eye started feeling a little gritty and watery too.
The whole white part of my right eye is pink and bloodshot, not just one isolated red dot or a dark ring right around the colored part.
It feels like burning and there is a gritty sensation like sand is trapped under my eyelid, but I don't have deep throbbing eye ache.
My eyesight is completely normal, though everything looks a bit blurry when tears pool up in my eye until I blink them away.
Bright light makes my eye water more and feels uncomfortable, but looking at a light does not trigger sharp or severe pain.
No, I have not seen any halos or rainbow rings around lights, and I do not have a headache, nausea, or vomiting.
The discharge is clear and watery like continuous tearing; my eyelids felt slightly sticky this morning, but they were definitely not glued shut with thick yellow pus.
It feels much more like burning and stinging than itching; it is not intensely itchy.
Yes, I felt a small swollen lump right in front of my right ear two days ago, and it is tender whenever I touch it or wash my face.

history.answer: My right eyelids are slightly swollen and puffy, but there is no painful stye or crusting along the edge of my eyelids.
No, moving my eyes around does not hurt at all, my eyes are not bulging outward, and I don't have any double vision.

exam.finding: Blood pressure 120/78 mmHg, heart rate 74 beats per minute, respiratory rate 14 breaths per minute, temperature 37.1°C, and oxygen saturation 99% on room air.
Alert and oriented female in no acute distress, with visible redness and watery tearing in the right eye, gently dabbing her cheek with a tissue.

Diffuse palpebral and bulbar conjunctival injection with follicular prominence on lower tarsal conjunctiva and clear watery discharge in the right eye; mild conjunctival injection in the left eye; no ciliary injection or subconjunctival hemorrhage.

Visual acuity is 20/20 in both eyes; pupils are equal, round, and reactive to light with no afferent pupillary defect; extraocular movements are full without pain or diplopia; corneas are clear bilaterally with no epithelial defect on fluorescein staining; no foreign body on upper eyelid eversion.
Tender, discrete, mobile lymph node measuring approximately 1 cm palpated in the right preauricular region; no cervical or submandibular lymphadenopathy.
Mild pharyngeal erythema without exudate; nasal mucosa shows mild clear congestion without purulent drainage.
No vesicles, crusts, rashes, or ulcerations on the forehead, eyelids, bridge or tip of the nose, or face.
